mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds continuously without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no significant correlation with 20-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% per annum signals an imminent monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a deteriorating consumer demand environment, triggering a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and HOUST falls > 10k in 3 months
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and HOUST falls > 10k in 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions (characterized by strong GDP growth and low unemployment), a sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% annually signals inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (as defined by GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 5.0%), a CPIAUCSL rise > 2.0% annually fails to produce negative 60-day forward returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index, 2017=100) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO falling below 100 fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% indicates weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rising above 5.5% fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-shock recovery regime (defined by a 10%+ drop in S&P 500 in the prior 30 days), a sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% monthly growth signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-shock recovery regime, RSAFS rising above 0.5% monthly fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and INDPRO falls > 1.0 in 3 months
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and INDPRO falls > 1.0 in 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns.
